title: Geometric branch count of a normal crossings divisor
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $D\subseteq X$ a closed subscheme represented by its quasi-coherent ideal. A pointed normal-crossings presentation of $D$ at $x\in X$ consists of an etale morphism $e:W\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a point $w$ over $x$, an affine open $U\ni w$, a Noetherian local ring $\mathcal O_{W,w}$, a regular system of parameters $t$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], and a sublist $s$ of $t$ such that the extended stalk ideal of $D\times_XW$ is $(\prod s)$. Its branch count is the length of $s$: all these factors lie in the maximal ideal, so exactly these factors vanish in the geometric prime. Write $A_D(x)$ for the set of these lengths and define $b_D(x)=\inf A_D(x)$ in $\mathbf N$, with the empty-set value $0$. For a normal crossings divisor [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor] these lengths agree, and this gives its number of geometric local branches. For a geometric point $p:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, put $b_D(p)=b_D(p(*))$, where $*$ is the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$.
